title: All 7 dome and cover-calibrator node types are dead: they always fail with 'No dome connected' even when the device is connected AND assigned to the saved profile
what_happened: Ran a sequence of [Open Dome, Close Dome, Park Dome, Park Mount] with the Simulated Dome connected. Open Dome failed 6 times in a row with 'Open Dome failed: No dome connected', each retry logged '[RECOVERY] Open Dome promoted device disconnect to recovery', and the whole run aborted 2s in. The Equipment screen at the same moment showed 'DOME  Simulated Dome  Connected' and the header read '7 connected'. I then saved the dome into the active equipment profile (equipment_profiles.dome_id = 'sim_dome_1', verified by sqlite3) and re-ran: identical failure. Root cause at source: runtime_config_operations.dart:84-91 calls backend.sequencerSetDevices(cameraId, mountId, focuserId, filterwheelId, rotatorId) and there is no dome or cover-calibrator parameter anywhere in the contract (roles/sequencer_backend.dart:92-100). The Rust executor exposes set_dome()/set_cover_calibrator() (executor/setup.rs:149,155) but grep shows no caller outside tests, so ctx.dome_id / ctx.cover_calibrator_id are permanently None and instructions.rs:544,551 always return the failure. This kills OpenDome, CloseDome, ParkDome, OpenCover, CloseCover, CalibratorOn and CalibratorOff — 7 of the 37 node types — on every platform, with or without hardware.
expected: With a connected (or profile-assigned) dome, Open Dome should command the dome. If no dome is available the app should say so before the run (preflight raised no equipment error for these nodes at all).
repro: Equipment > Discovery > connect Simulated Dome (and Edit Profile > Add from connected > Save). Sequencer > Builder > add Open Dome + Close Dome > Start > Start Anyway.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-35-dome.png (Session Report: 'Open Dome: No dome connected' x6), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-36-domeconnected.png (Equipment: Simulated Dome Connected, '7 connected'), app.log 16:24:18 and 16:53:17 (second run, after profile save)
proposed_fix: Add domeId, coverCalibratorId (and weather/safety/switch) to sequencerSetDevices across the backend roles + FFI, populate them from domeStateProvider/coverCalibratorStateProvider the same way rotatorId is, and call executor.set_dome()/set_cover_calibrator(). Until then, add a preflight ERROR when a sequence contains any dome/cover node.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on my own profile. Connected Simulated Dome (app.log 17:28:55 'Simulator connected: id=sim_dome_1 type=Dome', Equipment header '4 connected'), added a single Open Dome node, Start Anyway. Log 17:30:33.680047 onward: 'Open Dome failed: No dome connected' x7 with '[RECOVERY] Open Dome promoted device disconnect to recovery' between each; run aborted ~1s in (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/verify-14-domefail.png). Source chain verified: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/roles/sequencer_backend.dart:92 declares sequencerSetDevices with only camera/mount/focuser/filterwheel/rotator; runtime_config_operations.dart:84 passes exactly those five; native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sequencer_api.rs:154 sequencer_set_devices likewise; grep across native/**/*.rs shows set_dome/set_cover_calibrator (executor/setup.rs:149,155) are DEFINED and never called outside tests, and node/context.rs:637-638 defaults both to None. So instructions.rs:540/551 dome_id()/cover_calibrator_id() can only ever return the failure. Profile assignment cannot help because no parameter exists. Two minor corrections to the write-up: (a) pre-flight is not silent — it emits an INFO 'Dome Operations Present — This sequence includes dome operations. Cannot verify dome connection at edit time' (verify-13-preflight.png); the finding's stronger phrasing 'raised no equipment error' is still accurate. (b) flat_wizard/panel.rs:94,151,211 also reads ctx.cover_calibrator_id, so the blast radius is wider than the 7 node types. P0 retained: it is a hard, permanent feature break on every platform, though it fails loudly rather than silently.

title: 'Wait for Time' with no time picked returns Success instantly — a silent no-op with no validation warning
what_happened: Added a Wait for Time node and left 'Wait Until' at its default empty state ('Select time...'). Pre-flight raised no issue for it. At runtime the log shows 'Executing child 3/3: Wait for Time' immediately followed by 'Child Wait for Time completed with status: Success' in the same millisecond (17:10:43.766494 -> 17:10:43.766505). No wait happened. Confirmed at source: rules/timing_rules.dart:17-18 does `if (waitUntil == null) continue;` so an unconfigured node produces no ValidationIssue at all.
expected: Either a preflight ERROR ('Wait for Time has no time set') or a runtime failure. The single most common use of this node is 'wait until astronomical dark before imaging'; silently skipping it starts the run in daylight.
repro: New sequence > add 'Wait for Time' > do not touch Wait Until > Start > Start Anyway. Node completes instantly.
proposed_fix: Emit a ValidationSeverity.error when WaitTimeNode.waitUntil == null (and when a Loop's repeatUntil is null under the RepeatUntil condition), and make the runtime fail rather than succeed.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Added a Wait for Time node, left Wait Until at 'Select time...' (node row honestly reads 'until (unset)'). Pre-flight (verify-43-pf2.png) listed only 'No Exposures' + a disk-space info — no issue for the unconfigured wait. Runtime, my app.log: 17:41:14.615986 '[PROGRESS_CB] Emitting NodeStarted: name=Wait for Time' -> 17:41:14.615998 'Child Wait for Time completed with status: Success'. 12 microseconds, no wait. Source confirms the named line: timing_rules.dart:17 `if (waitUntil == null) continue;`, and grep shows WaitTimeNode appears in exactly one file under providers/sequence/rules/, so no other rule covers it. Severity P1 stands — the canonical use is 'wait for astronomical dark', and skipping it starts the run in daylight.

title: Run Script shows 'Timeout 300 s' but stores null, so the node refuses to run: 'Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode'
what_happened: Added a Run Script node, set only the Script Path to a working /tmp script, left the Timeout field showing 300 (rendered as a real value, not grey placeholder). Run failed at 16:28:21 with 'Run Script failed: Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode' and the script never executed (target file absent). I then typed 60 into the same Timeout field and re-ran: the script executed and the node returned Success. So a Run Script node is unusable out of the box, and the panel states a timeout that is not stored. Three different numbers are shown for the same unset field on one screen: the editor prints `node.timeoutSecs ?? 300` (_misc_properties.dart:52), the Timing card right below it prints `${script.timeoutSecs ?? 30}s` (node_timing_section.dart:588), and the duration estimator uses `?? 60` (sequence_time_estimator.dart:189).
expected: Either the editor writes its displayed default into the node on creation, or the field shows an empty/placeholder state and preflight errors on it. All three surfaces must agree.
repro: New sequence > add Run Script > set Script Path only > Start > Start Anyway. Fails. Type any number into Timeout > re-run. Succeeds.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur.png at 12:27 (panel shows Timeout 300 and Timing 'Timeout 30s'); app.log 16:28:21.089822 (failure) and 16:29:14.398317 (Success after editing); /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/script-ran.txt only written on the second run
proposed_fix: Give ScriptNode a non-null default timeoutSecs (300) in the constructor, or have the palette factory seed it. Delete the two divergent `?? 30` / `?? 60` fallbacks.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Added Run Script, set only Script Path to a working /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes-verify/t.sh, left Timeout showing 300 (rendered in solid white, unlike the grey placeholders in Script Path and Arguments on the same panel — verify-68-scriptprops.png). Run: app.log 17:56:00.032158 'Running script: .../t.sh []' then 17:56:00.032225 ERROR 'Run Script failed: Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode'; the script's sentinel file was never created. All three divergent surfaces verified simultaneously on one screen: editor field '300' (_misc_properties.dart:52 `node.timeoutSecs ?? 300`), Timing card 'Timeout 30s' (node_timing_section.dart:588 `?? 30`), pre-flight Simulation 'Duration 1m' (sequence_time_estimator.dart:189 `_defaultScriptTimeoutSecs = 60`, used at :597). Root cause verified: ScriptNode.timeoutSecs is `final int?` with no default (equipment_timing_and_automation.dart:531,543) and node_palette.dart:504 creates a bare `ScriptNode()`; instructions.rs:6329 returns the exact failure on None.

title: The Notification example template the UI itself suggests (${frame}) always fails and aborts the entire run, and the reason is thrown away
what_happened: The Title field's own hint is `e.g. Frame ${frame} of ${target.name} done` (_capture_rich.dart:347). I used `AUDIT NOTIF ${frame}` as the title. At runtime: 'ERROR Notification title `AUDIT NOTIF ${frame}` failed interpolation: Variable `${frame}` cannot be resolved: frame number is only set inside an exposure burst' — the node returned Failure and the whole sequence aborted, so the Park Mount node after it never ran and the mount was left unparked and tracking. A Notification instruction can never be 'inside an exposure burst', so the suggested example is guaranteed to fail. Worse, the Session Report's Errors section said only 'Sequence failed' with no cause, and sequence_runs.stats_json recorded errorMessages:["Sequence failed"] — the specific interpolation error exists only in the log. (By contrast Open Cover / Open Dome / Start Guiding failures DO propagate their real text, so this is a Notification-specific loss.)
expected: Either ${frame} resolves to something sane outside a burst, or the hint text does not advertise a variable this node cannot use. A template typo should not abort the run and strand the mount; and the run record should carry the real error text.
repro: Add Notification, set Title to `AUDIT NOTIF ${frame}`, add Park Mount after it, Start. Run fails at the Notification; Park never runs.
evidence: app.log 2026-08-01T16:19:34.199771; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-32-done.png (Session Report Errors = 'Sequence failed' only); sqlite3 sequence_runs id=1 stats_json errorMessages
proposed_fix: Change the hint to variables valid in this scope; make interpolation failure a warning that sends the raw title rather than a run-aborting error; propagate the instruction's failure message into run stats like every other node does.
verdict_reasoning: Every link verified. The hint is on screen verbatim: 'e.g. Frame ${frame} of ${target.name} done' (verify-74-3nodes.png; _capture_rich.dart:347). resolver.rs:258-262 resolves 'frame' from frame.frame with the message 'frame number is only set inside an exposure burst'. node/instructions/notification.rs:39-49 constructs `EvaluationFrame::empty()` — its own comment says frame fields are None here — and on interpolation error does a bare `return NodeStatus::Failure`, aborting the run. That bare early return is also exactly why the cause is lost: it bypasses `log_and_get_status_with_context("Notification", &ctx)` at the bottom of the same function, which is the call every other instruction uses to record its error text. Confirmed downstream in the prior run's DB: sequence_runs id=1 stats_json errorMessages == ["Sequence failed"] with no cause. P1 stands: a UI-suggested template guarantees an aborted run and strands whatever safing nodes follow it.

title: The daylight gate blocks light frames only when a Target node is present — a targetless Take Exposures wrote 3 daylight LIGHT frames
what_happened: At 16:19 (Sun ~55 deg altitude) a sequence with no TargetHeader ran Take Exposures 3 x 2 s and wrote 3 IMAGETYP='Light' FITS files to disk with no gate at all. At 17:02, with the identical camera and sun position but the exposures under a TargetHeader, the runtime refused: 'Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure — Sun altitude 55.4 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg for on-sky light imaging.' Slew is gated the same way. So forgetting to add a Target node silently removes the daylight protection for the exposures themselves.
expected: The daylight gate should key off frame type (light), not off whether a target group happens to exist.
repro: Sequence A: Take Exposures only (no Target) -> captures in daylight. Sequence B: Target > Smart Exposure -> refused by daylight gate.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced decisively, and with the variable isolated better than the original report (same node type on both sides, not Take Exposures vs Smart Exposure). Site set to lat 40 / lon -105, Sun ~63 deg. Sequence A = a bare 'Take Exposures' (LIGHT, 60s) with no TargetHeader: app.log 17:47:01.815050 'Starting 60.0s exposure', 17:48:02 'Saving FITS image to .../untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits', three frames written to disk, no gate anywhere in the log. Sequence B = the SAME Take Exposures node nested under a TargetHeader: app.log 17:53:17.075500 'Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure — Sun altitude 62.8 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg for on-sky light imaging.' and the run failed. So the gate is keyed off the presence of a target group, not off frame type. Severity up-called from P2 to P1: this is a safety gate that a user disables by forgetting an unrelated node, and there is no warning that protection is off.
